newsitem.title: USA: U.S. late spot prods narrowly mixed after APIs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. late spot prods narrowly mixed after APIs.

text.p: U.S. spot products prices were narrowly mixed tracking after-hours ACCESS futures following new weekly API data showing a sizeable draw on distillates and a solid gain on gasoline stocks, players said.
Earlier, all eyes were on widening differentials on Gulf Coast distillates, with traders citing keen buying by a handful of major refiners throughout the day.

The firmer Gulf diffs were little affected by news in the afternoon that Colonial Pipeline had lifted its allocation for the rest of February on shipments of distillates from Refinery Row to New York Harbor.
The pipeline cited a lack of distillate demand in the East Coast due to seasonally mild temperatures so far this winter.
The API data showed distillate stocks shrinking by 4.9 million barrels for the week ending February 7, helping to nudge March ACCESS heat 0.25 cent higher to 62.20 cents a barrel.
Heating oil stocks grew by almost 200,000 barrels in the Northeast, the data said, amid continuing mild weather.
March ACCESS gasoline slipped 0.15 cent to 63.80 cents by 1730 EST (2230 GMT), depressed by API's estimate of a 3.4 million barrel build for the week.
